summary: A 1934 modified L-4 lookout in the Los Padres National Forest on a 20-foot steel tower; the cab has collapsed onto the platform, and sources differ on the date.

facts.design: Modified L-4 cab atop a 20-foot steel H-braced tower
facts.status_note: The cab has collapsed onto the tower platform; the steel tower still stands.

staffing.status: seasonal lookout opened in 1939; a 1970 reader comment says it was manned that year

access.note: A maintained dirt road reaches the top; a blog says it is not advised for passenger cars. The collapsed cab is not a place to climb.

visit.trail_note: A maintained dirt road reaches the top; the blog advises against passenger cars.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Los Padres National Forest

events.note: Modified L-4 cab on a 20-foot steel H-braced tower
Telephone line to the peak completed in January 1935
Lookout ordered open for the season after lightning storms; the first lookout opened that season
Cab failed structurally and collapsed, per the California Lookouts history page (December 2012); a 2011 blog post already calls the cab collapsed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 2011 blog says the lookout fell into disuse in the 1960s; a reader's comment on the same page says the reader was hired and lived there in the summer of 1970, when it was manned. Both are reported, with the comment labelled as one person's recollection.

All sources agree the cab has collapsed. They differ on the date: the 2011 blog calls it collapsed in recent years, while the California Lookouts history page dates the collapse to December 2012. The story reports the range rather than picking one.

notes_for_editor: County disagrees: the NHLR page says Ventura County, while the California Lookouts page and the FFLA county list say Santa Barbara County; the record says Ventura, so a human should check the county line before changing it (not proposed as a correction here). The 1970 staffing rests only on a reader comment. The asterisk on 'Standing*' in the FFLA list is not explained in the source text read. The AWS cabin's WWII-era date is not given beyond 'World War II'. Road conditions come from undated or older web pages and may have changed.
